## How tonal is each training noise?

Candidates (1) and (3) both say: tonality differs between the banks.
Measure it. Same tracks, same estimator, every noise.[^harm]

### The old check

The old check (`tonality.py`, the v2 bank audit) reads no audio.
It takes a payload's expected spectrum at one constant speed.
Its prominence: peak bin over the median of a nearby ring.
`line_stats` (R4 `line_width_db3`) reads a render but means speed-aligned frames.

So it never sees jitter, wander, label error or a real track.

### The new check

It reads audio on a real track. Take one rotor $r$, one order $k$.

1. Shift the clip down by $k f_r(t)$. $f_r(t)$ is the true speed.
2. A line that follows the speed now sits at 0 Hz.
3. Cut 2 s frames, hop 0.5 s. Bins are 0.5 Hz wide.
4. Keep the band $\pm k$ Hz. Take the median over frames and mics.
5. Prominence = median at 0 Hz minus median at the band ends.

The band ends are $0.75k$ to $k$ Hz on both sides. White noise
reads 0 dB. A clean comb on its own track reads over 40 dB.

- **Tracks.** 18 real validation clips, 8 s each, every rotor ≥ 20 rev/s.
  Six are DREGON `free-flight_nosource_room1`. Twelve are Michael's
  `FLY124`: standby, climb and cruise.
- **Sources.** Legacy, v2 and v3: the two fits, plus 16 entries of each bank.
- **Real.** The recordings of the same clips, read on their telemetry labels.

Labels carry errors. An error of $\delta$ rev/s moves order $k$ by $k\delta$ Hz.
So the real number is a lower bound. It is the grey band.

One catch. A legacy render does not ride its label. It rides label +
a static offset per rotor: median 0.6 rev/s, up to 3.9. That offset is
the legacy label error. So a legacy render is read on label + offset.
That is its true shaft.
<!-- source: results/noise_v3/harmonicity/prominence.json results.legacy_*[*].shaft_offset_rps, |offset| 0.004–3.861, median 0.584 (34 legacy sources x 4 rotors) -->

### The result

![**What you see:** median prominence per order, one panel per generation. Dashed = the two fits. Blue = easy bank, red = hard bank (16 entries each). Grey = the real recordings on their labels (band = 25–75 %). Dotted lines at 3, 6 and 10 dB. Every curve uses the same 18 clips.](noise-model-v3-latent-runaway/harm_prominence.png){#fig-harm-prominence}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-harm-prominence
#| tbl-cap: "Prominence per family. Median (dB) over clips × entries × rotors × the orders of the group. Share over 3 / 6 / 10 dB counts every (clip, entry, rotor, order), k = 1–24. Real = the recordings on their labels, a lower bound. Source: `harm_summary.json`."
HS = json.loads(Path("noise-model-v3-latent-runaway/harm_summary.json").read_text())
harm_names = {
    "real": "real (labels)",
    "legacy_fit": "legacy fits",
    "legacy_easy": "legacy easy bank",
    "legacy_hard": "legacy hard bank",
    "v2_fit": "v2 fits",
    "v2_easy": "v2 easy bank",
    "v2_hard": "v2 hard bank",
    "v3_fit": "v3 r3b fits",
    "v3_easy": "v3r3 easy bank",
    "v3_hard": "v3r3 hard bank",
}
rows = [
    "| family | $k$ 1–4 | $k$ 5–8 | $k$ 9–16 | $k$ 17–24 | > 3 dB | > 6 dB | > 10 dB |",
    "|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|",
]
for key, name in harm_names.items():
    g = HS["families"][key]["nosource"]["groups"]
    rows.append(
        f"| {name} | "
        + " | ".join(f(g[s]["median_db"], 1) for s in ("k1-4", "k5-8", "k9-16", "k17-24"))
        + " | "
        + " | ".join(pct(g["all"][f"frac_gt{t}"]) for t in (3, 6, 10))
        + " |"
    )
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

### What it says

- **Candidate 1 fails in its sharp form.** On a real track the legacy comb
  is the least tonal. Past $k = 2$ its orders stand at most 1.1 dB over
  the band ends.
- The tall legacy stems of @fig-i3 are wide bumps, not lines. In the
  median legacy entry, 96 % of order 3 is incoherent noise. That noise
  is a Lorentzian of half-width 4–17 Hz at $k = 8$. So if the legacy comb
  helps, loud wide bumps help. Sharp lines do not.
- **Candidate 3 fails.** The hard banks are not less tonal. The v2 hard
  bank is the most tonal noise here: 44 % of its orders pass 3 dB.
  Legacy hard: 10 %.
- The v3r3 hard bank matches its easy bank: 18 % and 18 %. Both beat
  legacy hard.
- Tonality ranks legacy < v3 < v2. The hard arms rank the other way:
  5.41, 7.01, 7.06 rev/s. The v3 arm there used the round-2 banks.

Two limits. The real audio reads 0.2 dB on its labels. The labels smear
it, so it cannot rank the models. And a network sees the legacy bank on
its labels too. Read that way, legacy hard drops to 0.15 dB.
